title: Sensex Rallies 965 Points as IT, Banking Stocks Defy Global Selloff
excerpt: Indian benchmarks closed sharply higher on Friday, with the Sensex jumping 1.25% and the Nifty crossing 24,334, powered by IT and financial heavyweights even as Asian and US markets tumbled.
body:
• Sensex surged 964.58 points (1.25%) to close at 78,151.45; Nifty 50 gained 261.55 points (1.09%) to settle at 24,334.30
  • IT stocks led the rally after Tech Mahindra's better-than-expected Q1 FY27 results; Nifty IT surged 2.3% on the day and 4.2% for the week
  • Private banks gained on expectations that an RBI overseas deposit scheme could attract $30 billion from NRIs
  • Indian markets defied a global rout that saw South Korea's KOSPI plunge 6.37% and Japan's Nikkei drop 4.4%

Indian equity markets surged on Friday, posting their strongest single-session gains in weeks, even as a brutal selloff swept through Asian bourses and Wall Street retreated on escalating US-Iran tensions and a global semiconductor rout. The BSE Sensex jumped 964.58 points, or 1.25%, to close at 78,151.45, while the NSE Nifty 50 climbed 261.55 points, or 1.09%, to settle at 24,334.30, according to The Hindu BusinessLine.

The rally was driven by concentrated buying in IT and financial heavyweights, while the broader market lagged. The Nifty Midcap 100 and Smallcap 100 declined 0.41% and 0.21% respectively, reflecting selective profit-booking outside index names.

Tech Mahindra Earnings Spark IT Surge

Information technology stocks were the session's standout performers. Tech Mahindra rose 3.4% to ₹1,563 after reporting Q1 FY27 revenue of ₹157.12 billion ($1.63 billion), beating analyst estimates of ₹154.76 billion, according to Reuters. The company posted constant-currency revenue growth of nearly 3% quarter-on-quarter, with broad-based expansion across its manufacturing and communications verticals.

Infosys climbed 3.3% to ₹1,117, HCLTech gained 3% to ₹1,221, and TCS advanced 2.5%. The Nifty IT index rose 2.3% to 29,381, bringing its weekly gain to 4.2%. Nomura raised its target price for Tech Mahindra to ₹1,600, saying the company is on track to outperform large-cap IT peers during FY27 and FY28, according to Outlook Business.

"Markets staged a strong advance on Friday and gained over a percent despite weak global cues...the Nifty closed near the day's high."

— Ajit Mishra, SVP Research, Religare Broking

"The Nifty IT index rose 2.3% to 29,381, bringing its weekly gain to 4.2%."

"The Nifty IT index rose 2.3% to 29,381, bringing its weekly gain to 4.2%."

Wipro was the exception, falling more than 3% after reporting subdued Q1 results, with constant-currency revenue declining 1.2% quarter-on-quarter.

Banking Stocks Eye NRI Deposit Windfall

Private banking stocks provided additional fuel. Public sector banks expect to raise around $30 billion from the Reserve Bank of India's special overseas deposit scheme targeting non-resident Indians, sources told The Hindu BusinessLine. The scheme is designed to bolster India's forex reserves at a time when the rupee is under pressure from elevated crude oil prices.

HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank, Axis Bank, and Kotak Mahindra Bank all traded higher ahead of their quarterly earnings announcements scheduled for Saturday.

Global Markets Crumble Around India

The Indian rally was all the more striking against a backdrop of global carnage. South Korea's KOSPI plunged 6.37% as Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix led a semiconductor-driven selloff. Japan's Nikkei 225 dropped 4.4%, losing 2,939 points. Hong Kong's Hang Seng fell 1.72%.

On Wall Street, the Nasdaq fell 1.47%, dragged down by chip stocks, while the S&P 500 declined 0.51%. Escalating US-Iran conflict pushed Brent crude above $85 a barrel, with tanker traffic through the Strait of Hormuz at two-month lows after consecutive US strikes on Iranian military infrastructure.

Diaspora Angle: NRI Deposits and Rupee Pressure

For NRIs, the RBI's overseas deposit scheme could present an opportunity, though elevated US bond yields have so far limited takeup. VK Vijayakumar of Geojit Investments noted that FCNR(B) deposit mobilisation has remained below expectations, making the rupee the worst-performing Asian currency of the week with a depreciation of over 1%. The rupee closed at 96.28 against the dollar, logging its sharpest weekly drop since May.

What's Next

Investor attention next week will pivot to earnings from Reliance Industries, HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank, and Axis Bank, all reporting over the weekend. Private lenders are expected to post healthy numbers.

"A gradual uptrend driven by the earnings season is expected, though crude at elevated levels and rupee weakness remain key risks to watch."

— Siddhartha Khemka, Motilal Oswal

With the Nifty finding consistent support near 24,000 — its 20-day moving average — Axis Securities noted that a decisive breakout above 24,500 is needed for bulls to regain control. The earnings season, crude oil trajectory, and the US-Iran standoff will determine whether Friday's surge marks the start of a broader recovery or a one-day reprieve.
image_caption: The Bombay Stock Exchange building on Dalal Street in Mumbai, home to Asia's oldest stock exchange. On Friday, the Sensex surged 965 points as IT and banking stocks powered Indian markets higher despite a global selloff.
nri_angle: The RBI's special overseas deposit scheme could attract $30 billion from NRIs, while the rupee's weekly decline and elevated US bond yields create a complex remittance and investment landscape for the diaspora.
